episode_title: Buy Term and Invest the Difference vs. Infinite Banking

real_qa.q: What is the key difference between buy term and invest the difference versus infinite banking strategy?
real_qa.r: Buy term and invest the difference views insurance and investing as either/or choices, requiring discipline to consistently invest the savings difference. Infinite banking is an and strategy: you build cash value inside a policy, borrow against that cash value to deploy into investments, while the cash value continues compounding. The original cash value remains inside the policy while borrowed capital works elsewhere, allowing you to leverage the same dollars multiple times rather than choosing between one or the other.
real_qa.requete: infinite banking vs buy term invest difference strategy

real_qa.q: In the buy term and invest the difference model versus infinite banking over 30 years, what was the final wealth difference in the real client example?
real_qa.r: In a real client case analyzed over 30 years with $20,000 annual contributions and 10% investment returns, the buy term and invest the difference approach resulted in $2.1 million, while infinite banking produced $2.7 million—approximately 30% more wealth. Additionally, the infinite banking approach generated $2 million more in death benefit, providing a larger legacy to pass down to the next generation.
real_qa.requete: buy term invest difference vs infinite banking 2.7 million example

real_qa.q: What is the critical behavioral challenge most people face when attempting the buy term and invest the difference strategy?
real_qa.r: The fundamental problem is that most people do not actually invest the difference consistently over time. You must have the discipline to avoid spending that money on lifestyle upgrades—your expenses tend to rise to your income level. Anthony notes he has never had a prospect actually calculate what the specific difference would be and commit to investing it, which is why the strategy fails in practice despite sounding good in theory.
real_qa.requete: why people fail buy term invest the difference behavioral

real_qa.q: Why does infinite banking allow for increasing investment capacity each year compared to buy term and invest the difference?
real_qa.r: With buy term and invest the difference, you can only reinvest the annual difference you're setting aside—capped at $20,000 in the example. With infinite banking, the cash value compounds from day one even while borrowed against for investments. By year 10, while the buy term investor was still limited to $20,000 annual investments, the infinite banking client could deploy $25,000 that year, growing to $30,000, then $40,000 in subsequent years as compounding accelerated the available capital.
real_qa.requete: infinite banking compounding advantage investment capacity growth

real_qa.q: What tax and income challenges does a surviving spouse face in retirement that make death benefit planning important?
real_qa.r: When one spouse dies, the surviving spouse's tax filing status changes from married filing jointly to filing single, which places them in a higher tax bracket—effectively doubling their tax burden. Simultaneously, they lose one Social Security payment and can only keep the greater of the two. This means expenses increase (higher taxes, potentially mortgage/debt payoff needs) while income decreases, making death benefit proceeds critical to maintain a respectable retirement standard.
real_qa.requete: surviving spouse tax bracket death benefit retirement planning

real_qa.q: What is the recommended progression model for building wealth through infinite banking?
real_qa.r: The progression is: earn money, build capital savings, leverage that capital against the policy, acquire cash flowing assets, then use that cash flow to repay any policy loans. This cycle repeats over and over. This differs from the conventional model of earning money, buying term, investing the difference, and hoping investment accounts grow passively. Infinite banking positions life insurance as the financing layer that continuously acquires investments.
real_qa.requete: infinite banking wealth building progression model cycle
